report.headline: Usage share projected to rise to 24.5% in the EuroLeague, but the true-shooting projection carries no signal because the model does not beat a trivial baseline on that metric

projection.text: Projected usage rate climbs from 21.2% in the 2010-11 NBA season to 24.5% in the EuroLeague, with an 80% prediction interval of 20.4% to 28.7% and a 95% interval of 18.2% to 30.9%.

risks.text: True shooting in the source season was 50.4%, 0.73 standard deviations below the NBA average that year, indicating shooting efficiency was already a weak point before the move.
A 16.7% turnover rate accompanies a projected usage increase to 24.5%, raising the risk that ball-handling volume outpaces control in a larger role.

The true-shooting projection of 55.9% cannot be trusted as information: the model's error (4.7%) matches the error of just predicting the league average, so no efficiency conclusion should be drawn from it.

Players who historically made this exact transition sat 0.31 standard deviations below their own league's average once selected for the move, a cohort effect that tempers how far this specific projection should be extrapolated.

strengths.text: Already ran a usage rate 0.23 standard deviations above the NBA average in the source season, and the model projects that share to grow further to 24.5% against a EuroLeague average of 20.3%.
Carried a heavy playmaking load, posting a 33.3% assist rate and 7.377 assists per 75 possessions in the source season.
The usage-rate model beats its best trivial baseline (3.3% error vs 4.3%) over 367 held-out transitions, so the usage projection itself rests on a track record of outperforming naive guessing.
The projection is grounded in a reasonably sized historical cohort of 115 NBA-to-EuroLeague transitions.

uncertainty.text: The 80% usage interval spans 8.3 points, about two standard deviations of the target league's usage distribution (sd 4.2%), so the model can rank this player against peers but cannot pin down his individual number; the true-shooting projection of 55.9% should not be used at all, since its out-of-fold error (4.7%) is no better than simply guessing the league mean (also 4.7%).
